sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: This episode has now been updated to clarify our analysis of the Latino vote in the election.
sentences.zh: 本期节目现已更新，以澄清我们对选举中拉丁裔选票的分析。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: What the results of the election taught us about the American electorate and about the polling that once again failed to correctly understand it.
sentences.zh: 选举结果教会了我们关于美国选民的什么，以及关于那些再次未能正确解读选民意向的民调的什么。

sentences.en: A conversation with my colleague, Nate Cohen.
sentences.zh: 与我的同事内特·科恩的对话。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, November 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月10日，星期二。

sentences.en: So, Nate, we want to have two conversations with you.
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，我们想和你进行两次对话。

sentences.en: The first is about what we learned from the vote, the results of this election, now that the race has been called.
sentences.zh: 第一次是关于我们从投票和选举结果中学到了什么，现在竞选结果已经揭晓。

sentences.en: And second is what we learned about why the polls were so off once again, including our own polling here at the Times and kind of have a reckoning on that front.
sentences.zh: 第二次是关于我们学到了为什么民调再次出现如此大的偏差，包括我们《时报》自己的民调，并对此进行一番反思。

sentences.en: Sounds good.
sentences.zh: 听起来不错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm sure it's going to be a total pleasure for you.
sentences.zh: 我相信这对你来说会非常愉快。

sentences.en: It will be.
sentences.zh: 确实会。

sentences.en: Let's start with the voters and how this historic turnout for both candidates broke down.
sentences.zh: 让我们从选民开始，看看两位候选人创纪录的投票率是如何分布的。

sentences.en: And perhaps the most intriguing group in this campaign and so far in the results are Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 或许这次竞选中最引人注目的群体，以及到目前为止结果中最引人注目的群体，是拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: So tell us what the final, final-ish data is telling you about Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们，最终或者说接近最终的数据告诉你关于拉丁裔选民的什么信息。

sentences.en: Well, I suspect that many listening right now have probably heard that Donald Trump fared quite well among Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我怀疑现在很多听众可能已经听说唐纳德·特朗普在拉丁裔选民中表现相当不错。

sentences.en: You learned that pretty quickly on election night when the results from Miami-Dade County and Florida come in.
sentences.zh: 当迈阿密-戴德县和佛罗里达州的结果出来时，你在选举之夜很快就知道了这一点。

sentences.en: And now that we've seen more detailed results from elsewhere in the country, I think we can safely say that Latino voters really swung to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 现在我们看到了全国其他地区更详细的结果，我认为我们可以肯定地说，拉丁裔选民确实转向了唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Estimates vary about Latino support for Trump in 2016, but it's somewhere in the 25% to 30% range.
sentences.zh: 关于2016年拉丁裔对特朗普的支持率估算各不相同，但大致在25%到30%之间。

sentences.en: This year, I mean, we're still waiting for all the numbers, but we're expecting that to look more like 35%.
sentences.zh: 今年，我的意思是，我们还在等待所有数据，但我们预计这个数字看起来更接近35%。

sentences.en: And there's been an important focus this year on the fact that the Latino vote is not a monolith and hence the divided support for Biden and Trump.
sentences.zh: 今年有一个重要的焦点，即拉丁裔选票并非铁板一块，因此对拜登和特朗普的支持存在分歧。

sentences.en: But what's remarkable about this year is that when you look at the results so far, this increase in support for the president is consistent all over the country.
sentences.zh: 但今年值得注意的是，当你观察到目前为止的结果时，这种对总统支持率的增长在全国范围内是一致的。

sentences.en: It's true in the agricultural regions of California, like the Imperial Valley.
sentences.zh: 在加州的农业地区，比如帝国谷，情况确实如此。

sentences.en: It's true in the border towns along the Rio Grande.
sentences.zh: 在格兰德河沿岸的边境城镇，情况确实如此。

sentences.en: It's true, as you know, in Cuban areas like Miami-Dade County, but it's also true in Puerto Rican areas or around Orlando and Kissimmee.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，在迈阿密-戴德县这样的古巴裔聚居区确实如此，但在奥兰多和基西米周边的波多黎各裔聚居区也确实如此。

sentences.en: And it seems it's even true in the northern cities like Philadelphia or Milwaukee, where Latino voters are usually the very most reliable for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来在费城或密尔沃基这样的北部城市也是如此，而拉丁裔选民通常是民主党最可靠的支持者。

sentences.en: And the magnitude of the improvement for the president is really significant.
sentences.zh: 总统支持率提升的幅度确实非常显著。

sentences.en: There are counties along the Rio Grande where Trump picked up 50 points.
sentences.zh: 在格兰德河沿岸的一些县，特朗普的支持率上升了50个百分点。

sentences.en: 50 points among just Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 仅仅在拉丁裔选民中就上升了50个百分点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you can't know for sure that there isn't some contribution of white voters in these counties, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，你当然不能确定其中没有白人选民的贡献。

sentences.en: But these are places where Latino voters make up the overwhelming majority of the electorate.
sentences.zh: 但这些地方的拉丁裔选民占选民总数的绝大多数。

sentences.en: And we can say the same thing for these Latino enclaves in Philadelphia or Milwaukee.
sentences.zh: 对于费城或密尔沃基的这些拉丁裔聚居区，我们也可以这么说。

sentences.en: The magnitude of the gains there, it's not as staggering as it is along the Rio Grande, but it's still really stark.
sentences.zh: 那里的增长幅度虽然不像格兰德河沿岸那么惊人，但依然非常明显。

sentences.en: 15, 10, 20-point gains for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普获得了15、10、20个百分点的增长。

sentences.en: So, Nate, how do you start to explain what is now a much broader phenomenon than perhaps many of us thought it would be on election night?
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，你如何开始解释这个现象？它现在比我们在选举之夜所想的要广泛得多。

sentences.en: Is this the story of Democrats failing to capture this vote?
sentences.zh: 这是民主党未能争取到这些选票的故事吗？

sentences.en: Or is this the story of Donald Trump succeeding in capturing it?
sentences.zh: 还是唐纳德·特朗普成功争取到这些选票的故事？

sentences.en: Is it both?
sentences.zh: 两者都有吗？

sentences.en: How are you thinking about this?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待这个问题的？

sentences.en: You know, the first thing I would just say is I think this is a place where reporting on the ground will be really helpful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我首先要说的是，我认为实地报道在这里会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: The polls struggle with Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 民调在拉丁裔选民方面遇到了困难。

sentences.en: You know, in a national survey, you only get 100 Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在全国性调查中，你只能接触到100名拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: It's difficult to amass a lot of Latino respondents to do the kind of deep dives that we can do on larger subgroups like white voters, for instance, who I'm sure we'll get to.
sentences.zh: 很难聚集大量的拉丁裔受访者来进行我们对其他较大子群体（比如白人选民，我相信我们稍后会谈到）所能做的那种深入研究。

sentences.en: As a general framing point, I would say that this election was about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 作为一个总体的框架，我会说这次选举是关于唐纳德·特朗普的。

sentences.en: It was a referendum on the president.
sentences.zh: 这是一场针对总统的公投。

sentences.en: Joe Biden did everything he could to make sure it was about the president.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登尽其所能确保选举是围绕总统展开的。

sentences.en: He stayed in his basement, as the Trump campaign often noted.
sentences.zh: 正如特朗普竞选团队经常指出的那样，他待在地下室里。

sentences.en: And so I am inclined to assume that when we see big shifts, that it reflects attitudes about the president, not Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以我倾向于认为，当我们看到巨大的转变时，它反映的是对总统的态度，而不是对乔·拜登的态度。

sentences.en: So we should read into this that the president successfully appealed over the last year or so to this group of voters.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该理解为，总统在过去一年左右的时间里成功地吸引了这群选民。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One thing I would point out is that there was always strong evidence that the economy was the president's strong suit in this election.
sentences.zh: 我要指出的一点是，一直有强有力的证据表明，经济是总统在这次选举中的强项。

sentences.en: And when you look at the results, not just for Latino voters, but also for other non-Hispanic voters,
sentences.zh: 当你观察结果时，不仅是拉丁裔选民，还有其他非西班牙裔选民，

sentences.en: it does seem to me that the president made his largest gains in less affluent areas.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，总统在不太富裕的地区获得了最大的增长。

sentences.en: It would not surprise me if that reflects the greater salience of the economy for economically vulnerable people compared to people who might have the privilege to vote on other issues like cultural issues or the president's conduct in office and so on.
sentences.zh: 如果这反映了经济对于经济脆弱人群的重要性，相比于那些可能有特权去投票关注其他议题（如文化议题或总统在任期间的行为等）的人，我一点也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: A second observation I would make is that, to me, this was not an election about immigration in the same way that the 2016 election was sort of about immigration.
sentences.zh: 我要提出的第二个观察是，对我来说，这次选举不像2016年选举那样是关于移民问题的。

sentences.en: Trump's pledge to build the wall, his comments, you know, on his very first day, he sought the presidency when he said that Mexicans were rapists and criminals and so on.
sentences.zh: 特朗普承诺修建隔离墙，他的言论，你知道，他在宣布竞选总统的第一天就说墨西哥人是强奸犯和罪犯等等。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton in 2016 really focused on immigration as one of her major critiques of the president.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿在2016年确实将移民问题作为她对总统的主要批评之一。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't say that was nearly so true in 2020.
sentences.zh: 我不会说在2020年情况依然如此。

sentences.en: I don't think immigration even came up in the first presidential debate.
sentences.zh: 我不认为移民问题甚至在第一次总统辩论中被提及。

sentences.en: So I think you can imagine that immigration became less salient to not just Hispanic voters, but all voters.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你可以想象，移民问题不仅对西班牙裔选民，对所有选民来说都变得不那么重要了。

sentences.en: But that was particularly consequential among Hispanic voters because I think we can at least hypothesize that many Latino voters in 2016 were skeptical of the president in part because of the way he talked about this issue.
sentences.zh: 但这在西班牙裔选民中尤其重要，因为我认为我们至少可以假设，许多拉丁裔选民在2016年对总统持怀疑态度，部分原因是他谈论这个问题的方式。

sentences.en: So the issue that might have hurt President Trump with Latino voters, immigration was far less prominent this time than four years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，那个可能在拉丁裔选民中伤害特朗普总统的议题——移民，这次比四年前要突出得多。

sentences.en: And the thing that would potentially help him the most with Latino voters, the economy,
sentences.zh: 而那个最有可能在拉丁裔选民中帮助他的议题——经济，

sentences.en: did seem to work in his favor insofar as Latino voters identified him with economic prosperity, especially pre-pandemic economic prosperity.
sentences.zh: 确实在某种程度上对他有利，因为拉丁裔选民将他与经济繁荣联系在一起，尤其是疫情前的经济繁荣。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And one final point I would make is that the president has always done really well among white voters without a degree.
sentences.zh: 我要提出的最后一点是，总统在没有大学学历的白人选民中一直表现得非常好。

sentences.en: His shtick has had appeal for that demographic group.
sentences.zh: 他的那一套对那个群体很有吸引力。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's just about policy.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这仅仅是关于政策。

sentences.en: I also think it's about his conduct.
sentences.zh: 我也认为这是关于他的行为。

sentences.en: I think that the Trump Act has appeal to a lot of people who haven't previously been terribly receptive to Republican politicians in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为特朗普的表演对许多以前对共和党政客不太感冒的人很有吸引力。

sentences.en: And I think that if we're honest,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果我们诚实的话，

sentences.en: that it's not always obvious why the president's appeal to white working class voters on the economy or in terms of his conduct and temperament would also have appeal to working class voters who are non-white,
sentences.zh: 总统在经济方面或在行为和气质方面对白人蓝领选民的吸引力，为何也会对非白人蓝领选民产生吸引力，这并不总是显而易见的，

sentences.en: whether they're black or Latino.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是黑人还是拉丁裔。

sentences.en: So I could cobble together a theory that sort of says that many of the things that appeal to white working class voters about Donald Trump may appeal to Hispanic voters as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以拼凑出一个理论，说许多吸引白人蓝领选民的东西也可能吸引西班牙裔选民。

sentences.en: But in 2016, that was obscured by his position on immigration.
sentences.zh: 但在2016年，这被他在移民问题上的立场掩盖了。

sentences.en: And once immigration was sort of taken out of the picture,
sentences.zh: 一旦移民问题从画面中移除，

sentences.en: maybe that gave the president a belated opportunity to make the same sort of gains among working class Latino voters in 2020
sentences.zh: 也许这给了总统一个迟来的机会，在2020年在蓝领拉丁裔选民中取得同样的增长，

sentences.en: that he was able to make among white working class, traditionally Democratic voters in 2016.
sentences.zh: 就像他在2016年在白人蓝领、传统民主党选民中取得的那样。

sentences.en: It's interesting, Nate, that you made that parallel because as you were describing what's happening here, it occurred to me that if you are the Democratic Party,
sentences.zh: 内特，你做出这个类比很有趣，因为当你描述这里发生的事情时，我想到如果你是民主党，

sentences.en: the last major group of voters that were perhaps taken for granted in the past decade or so were white working class voters, especially in the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 过去十年左右可能被视为理所当然的最后一批主要选民群体是白人蓝领选民，特别是在中西部。

sentences.en: Democratic leaders kind of thought those voters were unquestioningly theirs.
sentences.zh: 民主党领导人认为这些选民毫无疑问是他们的。

sentences.en: I wonder if that's the right way of thinking about how the Democratic Party saw Latino voters in 2020,
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否是思考民主党在2020年如何看待拉丁裔选民的正确方式，

sentences.en: that there was an assumption that they would be with Joe Biden and they just were not to the same degree.
sentences.zh: 即有一种假设认为他们会支持乔·拜登，但他们并没有达到同样的程度。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是对的。

sentences.en: I think there are a lot of people in this country who became Democrats during an era when the Democratic Party was the party of working people
sentences.zh: 我认为这个国家有很多人在民主党是工薪阶层政党、共和党是富人和商业利益政党的时代成为了民主党人，

sentences.en: and the Republicans were the party of the rich and business interests who, over the last four years, have come to see the president as a different kind of Republican.
sentences.zh: 而在过去四年里，他们开始将总统视为一种不同类型的共和党人。

sentences.en: And the president has denied the Democrats some of their traditional advantage among working class voters of all races as a result.
sentences.zh: 结果，总统剥夺了民主党在各族裔蓝领选民中的部分传统优势。

sentences.en: This was not a campaign about privatizing Social Security.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场关于私有化社会保障的竞选。

sentences.en: It wasn't a campaign about the minimum wage and so on.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场关于最低工资等的竞选。

sentences.en: Instead, the Democrats have advanced a sort of idealistic liberal message with obvious resonance, at least, among college-educated voters.
sentences.zh: 相反，民主党提出了一种理想主义的自由派信息，至少在受过大学教育的选民中具有明显的共鸣。

sentences.en: And it didn't have the same resonance among working class voters.
sentences.zh: 而在蓝领选民中并没有产生同样的共鸣。

sentences.en: And Democrats in the past have gotten away with it by falling back on their traditional strength among these groups,
sentences.zh: 民主党过去通过依靠这些群体中的传统优势来蒙混过关，

sentences.en: longstanding allegiance that has maybe been eroded now that the Republicans have put forward a more populist candidate.
sentences.zh: 这种长期的忠诚度可能在共和党推出更民粹主义的候选人后受到了侵蚀。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Nate, what about black voters?
sentences.zh: 内特，那黑人选民呢？

sentences.en: What did we learn about this population from the results of Biden's victory?
sentences.zh: 我们从拜登获胜的结果中了解到了关于这个群体的什么？

sentences.en: I think that there were a few—that I would make a few points about what happened with black voters.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几点——关于黑人选民发生的事情，我会提出几点看法。

sentences.en: One is that it seems to me that although black turnout increased, it did not increase to the same extent as it increased among non-black voters.
sentences.zh: 第一，在我看来，尽管黑人投票率有所增加，但其增加幅度并没有像非黑人选民那样大。

sentences.en: And so as a result, the black share of the electorate seemed to decline.
sentences.zh: 因此，黑人在选民中的比例似乎有所下降。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The number of black Americans who voted did increase, but the number of everybody else increased just a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 投票的黑人美国人数量确实增加了，但其他所有人的数量增加得更多一点。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you may recall that in 2016, the turnout in places like Milwaukee and Philadelphia and Detroit was down, and it was down by so much that Hillary Clinton narrowly loSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能记得在2016年，密尔沃基、费城和底特律等地的投票率下降了，而且下降幅度之大导致希拉里·克林顿以微弱劣势落败。

sentences.en: In 2020, the turnout was up significantly, enough that if you could go back in time with this black turnout,
sentences.zh: 在2020年，投票率显著上升，足以让你如果能带着这种黑人投票率回到过去，

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton would have been the president.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿就会成为总统。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But yet the white turnout elsewhere in these states increased by even more, such that if you could go back in time and increase white turnout in 2016 to the same extent,
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，这些州其他地方的白人投票率增加得更多，以至于如果你能回到过去，将2016年的白人投票率增加同样的幅度，

sentences.en: Donald Trump would then come back and be president again.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普就会回来再次成为总统。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That is actually fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这真的很迷人。

sentences.en: You're saying if you applied the increase in both the black and white vote that occurred this year back then, you'd get the same result.
sentences.zh: 你是说如果你把今年黑人和白人投票率的增长应用到当时，你会得到同样的结果。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the end, the black versus white turnout dynamic did not change in a way that would have allowed the Democrats to prevail four years ago.
sentences.zh: 最终，黑人与白人的投票率动态并没有以一种允许民主党在四年前获胜的方式改变。

sentences.en: And among the black voters who turned out, what percentage supported Biden versus President Trump?
sentences.zh: 在参与投票的黑人选民中，有多少比例支持拜登，多少支持特朗普总统？

sentences.en: Because I have the sense that the president did somewhat better with black voters than was expected.
sentences.zh: 因为我有一种感觉，总统在黑人选民中的表现比预期的要好一些。

sentences.en: I think that's right to an extent.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上是这样。

sentences.en: I think that this is, again, a case where we'll need to see the final data before we nail this down.
sentences.zh: 我认为这又是一个我们需要在看到最终数据后才能确定的案例。

sentences.en: But let's just say that Biden won roughly 90 percent of the black vote and that Donald Trump won around 10 percent of the black vote, give or take.
sentences.zh: 但我们假设拜登赢得了大约90%的黑人选票，而唐纳德·特朗普赢得了大约10%的黑人选票，上下浮动。

sentences.en: You know, we'll see what the final numbers are.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们会看到最终数字是多少。

sentences.en: That will be better for Donald Trump than in 2016.
sentences.zh: 这对唐纳德·特朗普来说将比2016年更好。

sentences.en: And if I were forced to explain it, I would chalk up a similar explanation to what I told you with Latino voters
sentences.zh: 如果我被迫解释它，我会归结为一个与我告诉你的关于拉丁裔选民类似的解释，

sentences.en: where some combination of the president's economic appeal and so on was able to help him peel off just a little bit.
sentences.zh: 即总统的经济吸引力等因素的某种组合使他能够争取到一点点支持。

sentences.en: But I don't want to overthink it too much.
sentences.zh: 但我不想过度解读。

sentences.en: This is a pretty small shift, all things considered.
sentences.zh: 考虑到所有因素，这是一个相当小的转变。

sentences.en: And the Democrats continue to command the overwhelming support of black voters.
sentences.zh: 而且民主党继续掌握着黑人选民的压倒性支持。

sentences.en: Nate, if your theory is accurate and what connects the improvement by Donald Trump among Latino and black voters is his economic message,
sentences.zh: 内特，如果你的理论是准确的，并且唐纳德·特朗普在拉丁裔和黑人选民中改善的原因是他的经济信息，

sentences.en: what's interesting about that, of course, is that the economy is doing terribly right now because of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当然，有趣的是，由于疫情，经济现在表现得很糟糕。

sentences.en: And so it means that there's kind of a vestigial affection for the president's success, you know, a year ago, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着对总统过去一年成功的某种残余情感，你知道，对吧？

sentences.en: The way the stock market did before the pandemic, the way job growth was going before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 疫情前股市的表现，疫情前就业增长的趋势。

sentences.en: But it's remarkable that he's still getting credit for that given where things are right now.
sentences.zh: 但令人瞩目的是，考虑到目前的情况，他仍然因为这些而获得认可。

sentences.en: Here are the points I would make.
sentences.zh: 以下是我要提出的观点。

sentences.en: One, you're totally right.
sentences.zh: 第一，你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: I think that the president does still get credit for the way he handled the economy during ordinary circumstances.
sentences.zh: 我认为总统在普通情况下处理经济的方式仍然得到认可。

sentences.en: And people can rationally believe that the president was a good steward of the economy when coronavirus wasn't in the picture.
sentences.zh: 人们可以理性地认为，在没有新冠病毒的情况下，总统是经济的良好管理者。

sentences.en: And therefore, he'll be a good steward of the economy once coronavirus is out of the picture.
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦新冠病毒消失，他也会成为经济的良好管理者。

sentences.en: The second thing I would say is that I think that he also has gotten some credit from people for the way he handled the economy during the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 我要说的第二点是，我认为他还因为在新冠病毒期间处理经济的方式而获得了一些认可。

sentences.en: The stimulus package was really popular.
sentences.zh: 刺激计划非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: The Democrats have not criticized the way he's handled the economy during the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 民主党并没有批评他在新冠病毒期间处理经济的方式。

sentences.en: They've only criticized his handling of the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 他们只是批评了他对新冠疫情的处理方式。

sentences.en: And even on his handling of the coronavirus, the main criticism of him is that he's too eager to reopen the economy.
sentences.zh: 即便是在处理新冠疫情的问题上，对他主要的批评也只是说他太急于重启经济了。

sentences.en: So it's a little bit complicated to make people go through the logic of here's someone who wants to reopen the economy and therefore is on the side of, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，要让人们理清这个逻辑有点复杂：这里有个人想重启经济，因此他站在了，你知道的，

sentences.en: getting people back to work and so on.
sentences.zh: 让人们重返工作岗位等等这一边。

sentences.en: But he's actually bad for the economy because that step that's facially good for the economy will contribute to the spread of the coronavirus for shutdowns, which hurt the economy.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他不利于经济，因为那个表面上对经济有利的举措，会助长新冠病毒的传播，从而导致封锁，而封锁会损害经济。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, I do think that we take that logic for granted in a way that I'm not sure we should expect of ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我确实认为我们以一种理所当然的态度看待这种逻辑，我不确定我们是否应该对普通民众有这样的期待。

sentences.en: Fair point.
sentences.zh: 说得有道理。

sentences.en: Okay, so I now want to turn to a group that we have been talking about a lot throughout this campaign, a group that was predicted to potentially be decisive in this election,
sentences.zh: 好的，现在我想转向我们在整个竞选过程中一直在讨论的一个群体，一个被预测可能在这次选举中起到决定性作用的群体，

sentences.en: and that was suburban voters.
sentences.zh: 那就是郊区选民。

sentences.en: Polls predicted that many of the suburban voters who had voted for Trump four years ago would swing to Biden.
sentences.zh: 民调预测，许多四年前投票给特朗普的郊区选民会转向拜登。

sentences.en: Did that end up happening?
sentences.zh: 结果真的发生了吗？

sentences.en: That's the thing that ended up happening.
sentences.zh: 这正是最终发生的事情。

sentences.en: And it was just enough for him to get over the top in the northern battleground states as well as in Arizona and in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 而且这足以让他不仅在北部摇摆州，还在亚利桑那州和佐治亚州胜出。

sentences.en: Across the country, Joe Biden did better in suburban areas than Hillary Clinton did four years ago.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，乔·拜登在郊区的表现比四年前的希拉里·克林顿更好。

sentences.en: His gains were largest in traditionally Republican suburban areas like Atlanta, like Dallas, like Jacksonville, Indianapolis, Kansas City, Grand Rapids, Michigan.
sentences.zh: 他的增长主要集中在传统的共和党郊区，比如亚特兰大、达拉斯、杰克逊维尔、印第安纳波利斯、堪萨斯城和密歇根州的大急流城。

sentences.en: Places that are not full of liberal suburbanites that have been voting Democratic for a really long time, like, you know, Westchester County or the suburbs of D.C.
sentences.zh: 这些地方不像威彻斯特县或华盛顿特区周边那样，充斥着长期投票支持民主党的自由派郊区居民，

sentences.en: and Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 也不像费城的郊区。

sentences.en: And don't get me wrong, Biden did make gains in a lot of those traditionally Democratic suburban areas.
sentences.zh: 别误会，拜登确实在许多传统的民主党郊区也取得了增长。

sentences.en: But the biggest gains were in the areas where 10 or 15 years ago the Republicans dominated among the suburban vote.
sentences.zh: 但最大的增长出现在那些10到15年前共和党在郊区选票中占据主导地位的地区。

sentences.en: And now a lot of traditionally Republican affluent white voters in those areas are saying, wait a second,
sentences.zh: 而现在，这些地区许多传统的共和党富裕白人选民在说，等一下，

sentences.en: this isn't the Republican Party I signed up for and now have swung pretty decisively to the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我所支持的那个共和党，于是他们相当果断地转向了民主党。

sentences.en: And do we know why there was this shift?
sentences.zh: 我们知道为什么会出现这种转变吗？

sentences.en: It feels like that word you just used, affluence, may be an element of it,
sentences.zh: 感觉你刚才用的那个词“富裕”可能是一个因素，

sentences.en: that these are voters who can financially afford to cast a vote based on whether they like Trump or Biden.
sentences.zh: 这些选民在经济上有能力根据自己是否喜欢特朗普或拜登来投票。

sentences.en: Yeah, I definitely think there's something to that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我绝对认为这其中有一定道理。

sentences.en: You know, I think that there are a lot of rich white people in the suburbs of Dallas, in the suburbs of Atlanta, who have been voting for their tax cuts for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为在达拉斯和亚特兰大的郊区有很多富有的白人，他们长期以来一直投票支持减税。

sentences.en: But Donald Trump crossed a line with them in terms of his personal conduct.
sentences.zh: 但唐纳德·特朗普在个人品行方面触碰了他们的底线。

sentences.en: And they are willing to vote on what they feel and think about him as a person in a way that maybe other people are not necessarily so inclined to do.
sentences.zh: 他们愿意根据自己对他的个人感受和看法来投票，而其他人可能未必有这种倾向。

sentences.en: I also do think there is a policy element of it as well.
sentences.zh: 我也认为这其中还有政策因素。

sentences.en: I think that immigration has always been popular and free trade has always been popular among a big chunk of conservative voters in suburbs across the South.
sentences.zh: 我认为移民和自由贸易在南方各州郊区的大部分保守派选民中一直很受欢迎。

sentences.en: And the president has departed from traditional Republican views on some of those issues in a way that may at least somewhat complicate the idea that this is strictly a vote against their policy views.
sentences.zh: 而总统在其中一些问题上背离了传统的共和党观点，这可能至少在一定程度上让“这纯粹是反对其政策观点”的说法变得复杂。

sentences.en: But I do think it's true that it's a lot easier for someone making $200,000 a year to vote against their perceived economic interests than it would be if you make $20,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，对于一个年收入20万美元的人来说，投票反对他们认为的经济利益，要比年收入2万美元的人容易得多。

sentences.en: Okay, so finally, what about white, non-college educated voters, many of whom are in rural America, not suburban?
sentences.zh: 好的，最后，那些没有大学学历的白人选民呢？他们许多人住在农村，而不是郊区。

sentences.en: So we may be talking about ex-urban or rural voters.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的可能是远郊或农村选民。

sentences.en: This is traditionally seen as the president's base.
sentences.zh: 这传统上被视为总统的票仓。

sentences.en: This is the group that Biden had hoped he would start to poach.
sentences.zh: 这是拜登曾希望开始争取的群体。

sentences.en: How successfully did he do that?
sentences.zh: 他做得有多成功？

sentences.en: How well did President Trump defend this space for himself according to the data that you have seen?
sentences.zh: 根据你看到的数据，特朗普总统在捍卫这一阵地方面表现如何？

sentences.en: Donald Trump defended his base here and to a far greater extent than any of the pre-election polls anticipated.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在这里捍卫了他的票仓，而且程度远超选前任何民调的预期。

sentences.en: As far as I can tell, Joe Biden didn't make any gains in rural America among white voters since 2016.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，自2016年以来，乔·拜登在农村地区的白人选民中没有任何增长。

sentences.en: And as you alluded to, the whole sort of premise of choosing Scranton Joe was that if the Democrats nominated a white moderate with some populist appeal,
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，选择“斯克兰顿的乔”的整个前提是，如果民主党提名一位具有民粹主义吸引力的温和派白人，

sentences.en: that you could win back some of the voters who backed Barack Obama in 2012, supported Donald Trump in 2016.
sentences.zh: 那么你就能赢回一些在2012年支持巴拉克·奥巴马，而在2016年支持唐纳德·特朗普的选民。

sentences.en: And that just didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有发生。

sentences.en: And in many cases, Donald Trump extended his gains.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，唐纳德·特朗普反而扩大了他的优势。

sentences.en: There are places in rural Iowa and rural Ohio where Donald Trump did even better than he did four years ago.
sentences.zh: 在爱荷华州和俄亥俄州的农村地区，唐纳德·特朗普的表现甚至比四年前还要好。

sentences.en: And that is just the exact opposite of what the pre-election poll said.
sentences.zh: 这与选前民调的结果完全相反。

sentences.en: So something went very wrong in the public opinion research there.
sentences.zh: 所以那里的公众舆论研究出了大问题。

sentences.en: Well, we will get to that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: But Nate, at the end of the day, if I'm putting all these pieces together the way I think you have intended for me to,
sentences.zh: 但是内特，归根结底，如果我按照你预想的方式把这些碎片拼凑起来，

sentences.en: it feels like suburban voters end up being the most important group to shift and shift in the direction of Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 感觉郊区选民最终成了最关键的转变群体，而且是向乔·拜登方向的转变。

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: We have known for a very long time that voters had deep reservations about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我们早就知道选民对唐纳德·特朗普有很深的保留意见。

sentences.en: We know that he only received 46 percent of the national vote in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他在2016年全国选票中只获得了46%。

sentences.en: We know that he was the least popular candidate in terms of favorability ratings when he was elected.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他在当选时是支持率最低的候选人。

sentences.en: And the president had four years to try and address those shortcomings.
sentences.zh: 总统有四年的时间来尝试解决这些不足。

sentences.en: It seems that his handling of the economy and his performance on the job was enough to persuade some number of more economically vulnerable voters,
sentences.zh: 看来他对经济的处理和他的工作表现足以说服一些经济上更脆弱的选民，

sentences.en: or maybe just voters in general, even higher on the economic spectrum, to support his re-election despite the personal reservations that they've probably had about him for years.
sentences.zh: 或者也许只是普通的选民，甚至是经济阶层更高的选民，去支持他的连任，尽管他们多年来可能对他一直有个人保留意见。

sentences.en: But it also seems that in nominating Joe Biden, someone who was fairly broadly appealing and who promised to unify the country and to act in a way more befitting of the office,
sentences.zh: 但似乎通过提名乔·拜登，一个相当广泛地受欢迎、承诺团结国家并以更符合总统身份的方式行事的人，

sentences.en: that Joe Biden was able to consolidate a significant number of voters who have had longstanding reservations about the president,
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登能够巩固大量对总统长期持有保留意见的选民，

sentences.en: especially college-educated voters, especially traditionally Republican-tilting independent voters in the suburbs around many of our largest cities.
sentences.zh: 特别是受过大学教育的选民，特别是我们许多大城市周边郊区那些传统上倾向共和党的独立选民。

sentences.en: And that, to me, tells you a very odd and interesting story.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说，讲述了一个非常奇怪且有趣的故事。

sentences.en: It says that the economy can really help the president, as we've already known, but there are limits to it.
sentences.zh: 它说明经济确实可以帮助总统，正如我们已经知道的那样，但这是有限度的。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Let's take a look at our new poll, and the headline number is this.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看我们的新民调，头条数字是这个。

sentences.en: This is a wow.
sentences.zh: 这真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: The largest lead of the race for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登在竞选中取得了最大的领先优势。

sentences.en: Joe Biden with a 14-point lead nationally over President Trump.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登在全国范围内领先特朗普总统14个百分点。

sentences.en: 10 points.
sentences.zh: 10个百分点。

sentences.en: 12-point lead over Trump.
sentences.zh: 领先特朗普12个百分点。

sentences.en: The largest lead of the race for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登在竞选中取得了最大的领先优势。

sentences.en: But 16-point spread.
sentences.zh: 但有16个百分点的差距。

sentences.en: Joe Biden leads in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登在密歇根州领先。

sentences.en: He leads in North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 他在北卡罗来纳州领先。

sentences.en: He leads in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他在宾夕法尼亚州领先。

sentences.en: He leads in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 他在威斯康星州领先。

sentences.en: Joe Biden is leading President Trump by 11 points in Wisconsin in the latest New York Times-Siena college poll.
sentences.zh: 在最新的《纽约时报》与锡耶纳学院民调中，乔·拜登在威斯康星州领先特朗普总统11个百分点。

sentences.en: Joe Biden is in the hunt in these races that have been going red of late in these states.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登在这些近期转向共和党的州中也处于竞争状态。

sentences.en: So imagine Joe Biden's election night could also include North Carolina, could possibly include Florida.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，乔·拜登的选举之夜可能还会包括北卡罗来纳州，甚至可能包括佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: This is not an out-of-the-question map here for Joe Biden, given the state of the race.
sentences.zh: 考虑到目前的竞选态势，这对乔·拜登来说并非不可能。

sentences.en: So Nate, now for the root canal section of this conversation.
sentences.zh: 那么内特，现在进入我们谈话中“根管治疗”的部分。

sentences.en: You cover polling for the Times, and you are involved in how polling itself is conducted for and by the Times, along with our partners.
sentences.zh: 你负责《时报》的民调报道，并且参与了《时报》及其合作伙伴进行民调的方式。

sentences.en: And we all know at this point that there was significant polling error this year.
sentences.zh: 我们现在都知道，今年出现了严重的民调误差。

sentences.en: How would you describe the level of polling error in 2020?
sentences.zh: 你会如何描述2020年的民调误差水平？

sentences.en: I would consider this to be far worse than 2016.
sentences.zh: 我认为这比2016年严重得多。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Far worse.
sentences.zh: 严重得多。

sentences.en: In terms of the difference between the final poll results and the actual results, the difference is not that much worse than 2016.
sentences.zh: 就最终民调结果与实际结果的差异而言，差异并不比2016年大多少。

sentences.en: It's pretty comparable.
sentences.zh: 相当可比。

sentences.en: But pollsters this year do not have the same excuses that they had four years ago.
sentences.zh: 但今年的民调机构没有四年前那样的借口了。

sentences.en: And I think that the error is much more systematic and betrays much more fundamental problems with the effort to represent the electorate than the polling did four years ago.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种误差更具系统性，且比四年前的民调暴露了更多关于代表选民意愿这一努力的根本性问题。

sentences.en: And I want you to give us some examples, just so we are on the same page.
sentences.zh: 我想让你举几个例子，好让我们达成共识。

sentences.en: When you say the polls are worse this time than four years ago, what do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 当你说明年的民调比四年前更糟糕时，你指的是什么？

sentences.en: The – maybe it's easier to start with 2016 for a second.
sentences.zh: ——也许从2016年开始说起会更容易些。

sentences.en: The polls did a good job of representing white voters without a degree in that they showed white voters without a degree being great for Trump against Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 民调在代表没有大学学历的白人选民方面做得不错，因为它们显示这些选民在反对希拉里·克林顿方面非常支持特朗普。

sentences.en: But they did not have enough of those voters.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有足够的这类选民样本。

sentences.en: And although that is a serious problem in polling to not have enough of a certain demographic group,
sentences.zh: 虽然民调中缺乏某个特定人口群体是一个严重的问题，

sentences.en: it is a common problem in polling and it is a fixable problem because you can give more weight to voters from that demographic group.
sentences.zh: 但这在民调中是一个常见问题，也是一个可以解决的问题，因为你可以增加该人口群体选民的权重。

sentences.en: And in the post-election analysis four years ago, pollsters found that when they gave more weight to that group, that the polls did pretty well.
sentences.zh: 在四年前的选后分析中，民调机构发现，当他们增加该群体的权重时，民调表现相当不错。

sentences.en: In 2020, pollsters did that.
sentences.zh: 在2020年，民调机构这样做了。

sentences.en: They gave more weight to white working class voters, but they were no closer to the result.
sentences.zh: 他们增加了白人蓝领选民的权重，但结果并没有更接近实际。

sentences.en: Even though we know that the same technique four years ago would have brought the polls closer to the result.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们知道四年前同样的技术本可以使民调结果更接近实际。

sentences.en: So I just want to be clear on this.
sentences.zh: 所以我只想把这一点说清楚。

sentences.en: You're saying what makes the error in 2020 greater and more grievous than 2016 is that we entered 2020 having made meaningful adjustments to our polling methodology, all polls,
sentences.zh: 你是说，2020年的误差比2016年更大、更严重的原因是，我们在进入2020年时，已经对我们的民调方法（所有民调）进行了有意义的调整，

sentences.en: when it comes to the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 在总统选举方面。

sentences.en: And yet we still had super off polls despite those reforms and adjustments.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管进行了这些改革和调整，我们的民调依然错得离谱。

sentences.en: Not only were they super off, though, they were just as bad.
sentences.zh: 不仅错得离谱，而且和以前一样糟糕。

sentences.en: And what that means is that while four years ago the polls showed Donald Trump doing really well among white voters without a degree and had too few of them,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，虽然四年前民调显示唐纳德·特朗普在没有大学学历的白人选民中表现非常好，但样本太少，

sentences.en: this year the polls had the right number of white voters without a degree, but they showed Joe Biden doing way better among this group than he actually did.
sentences.zh: 而今年民调拥有了正确数量的此类选民，但它们却显示乔·拜登在该群体中的表现远好于实际情况。

sentences.en: So for all this election, we've been saying white voters without a degree who voted for Donald Trump in 2016 appear to have come back for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以整个选举期间，我们一直在说，2016年投票给唐纳德·特朗普的无大学学历白人选民似乎又回到了乔·拜登这边。

sentences.en: And that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有发生。

sentences.en: Okay, so how do you explain the level of error that you just ticked through after all the corrections made four years ago to try to ensure that this would never happen?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么在四年前为了确保这种情况不再发生而做出所有修正之后，你如何解释你刚才列举的误差水平？

sentences.en: I am going to try and answer your question.
sentences.zh: 我会试着回答你的问题。

sentences.en: But before I do that, I do want to say that it is too soon to have a definitive autopsy on this.
sentences.zh: 但在我回答之前，我想说现在对这件事进行最终的“尸检”还为时过早。

sentences.en: I mean, to take that analogy a little further, the body is still dead at the scene of the crime.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，把这个比喻再延伸一点，尸体还在犯罪现场。

sentences.en: It has not made it to the morgue yet for us to go into the details and dig in to see exactly what went on here.
sentences.zh: 它还没有送到停尸房，我们还无法深入细节去挖掘到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: I mean, we know the polls went really wrong, but it's going to be a bit until we've nailed down exactly why.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们知道民调出了大问题，但还需要一点时间才能确定具体原因。

sentences.en: But assuming you're a crime scene investigator and you're there and you're trying to figure it out, what do you know so far?
sentences.zh: 但假设你是犯罪现场调查员，你在现场试图弄清楚情况，你目前了解到了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I can just toss out some ideas, and that's all they are at this stage.
sentences.zh: 是的，我可以抛出一些想法，现阶段也只能是想法。

sentences.en: We have seen over the last four years a huge increase in political participation on the left.
sentences.zh: 过去四年里，我们看到左翼的政治参与度大幅增加。

sentences.en: We also know that political participation correlates with participating in polls, which makes sense.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道政治参与度与参与民调呈正相关，这很合理。

sentences.en: You get called and you either choose to take the survey or not.
sentences.zh: 你接到电话，要么选择接受调查，要么不接受。

sentences.en: And if that interests you because you're interested in politics, you're likelier to take a poll.
sentences.zh: 如果你因为对政治感兴趣而参与，那你更有可能接受民调。

sentences.en: Well, this could mean that Democrats became a little more likely to take a poll.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可能意味着民主党人变得更愿意接受民调了。

sentences.en: That's one possibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可能性。

sentences.en: Another possibility is to look at it on the other side, that Trump voters are less likely to respond to surveys than they were four years ago.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是从另一面看，即特朗普选民比四年前更不愿意回应调查。

sentences.en: Perhaps the president's attacks on the media and institutions have gradually eroded their trust in surveys.
sentences.zh: 也许总统对媒体和机构的攻击逐渐削弱了他们对调查的信任。

sentences.en: Maybe even the 2016 result itself had a role in diminishing their willingness to participate in surveys because the polls were off by so much that now they don't trust them and don't want to play.
sentences.zh: 也许2016年的结果本身也在削弱他们参与调查的意愿中起到了作用，因为当时的民调误差太大，以至于现在他们不信任民调，也不想参与了。

sentences.en: We make sure in the state of Pennsylvania that 41% of our interviews are with Republicans or whatever the number was in that area.
sentences.zh: 我们在宾夕法尼亚州确保了41%的受访者是共和党人，或者该地区的数字是多少。

sentences.en: Which Republicans picked up the phone?
sentences.zh: 哪些共和党人接了电话？

sentences.en: Were they the ones that were really enthusiastic about the president in rural areas?
sentences.zh: 是那些在农村地区对总统非常热情的选民吗？

sentences.en: Or were they the people who are also registered as Republican but are no longer fans of the president?
sentences.zh: 还是那些虽然注册为共和党人，但不再是总统粉丝的人？

sentences.en: I think that we have to conclude that we got the ones who are more likely not to be fans of the president.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须得出结论，我们得到的是那些不太可能是总统粉丝的人。

sentences.en: That's not to say we didn't get plenty of people who supported the president, but enough of a difference compared to reality that you nudge all the polls in one direction.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们没有得到大量支持总统的人，但与现实相比存在足够的差异，足以让所有民调向一个方向偏移。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, we've had four years of the president speaking about the organizations that conduct polling in a very specific way.
sentences.zh: 好吧，内特，总统已经连续四年以一种非常特定的方式谈论进行民调的机构了。

sentences.en: And that would be the New York Times, which conducts polls, that would be ABC News, that would be CNN, that would be CBS.
sentences.zh: 那就是进行民调的《纽约时报》、美国广播公司新闻部（ABC News）、美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）和哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）。

sentences.en: And he has described them as the enemy of the people.
sentences.zh: 他把他们描述为人民的敌人。

sentences.en: He has described them as fake media.
sentences.zh: 他把他们描述为假媒体。

sentences.en: So I don't have a hugely hard time understanding why his supporters would be skeptical of answering our calls.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不难理解为什么他的支持者会对回答我们的电话持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: No, I think that four years of the president advancing that message could have had a negative effect on the polls.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为总统四年来推进这一信息可能对民调产生了负面影响。

sentences.en: I think that's totally possible.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全有可能。

sentences.en: I don't have any proof of that, but what's important about that theory is that it could potentially explain why the polls have gotten worse since 2016.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何证据，但该理论的重要之处在于，它可能解释了为什么民调自2016年以来变得更糟。

sentences.en: That, to me, is the key part of any theory if you really want to try and dig into what's happening here.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，如果你真的想深入探究这里发生了什么，那才是任何理论的关键所在。

sentences.en: So, Nate, are we left with the kind of inevitable conclusion here after two presidential elections that pretty much committed the same sin, perhaps for different reasons,
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，在经历了两次几乎出于不同原因却犯下同样错误的总统大选后，我们是否得出了一个不可避免的结论，

sentences.en: that election polling, pre-election polling, is broken?
sentences.zh: 即选举民调，也就是选前民调，已经失效了？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: And I think it depends on the level of precision that you expect out of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这取决于你对它所要求的精确度。

sentences.en: And there's a spectrum of ways that you can interpret polling errors.
sentences.zh: 解读民调误差的方式有很多种。

sentences.en: One possibility is that the polls are imprecise, but they're still useful.
sentences.zh: 一种可能性是，民调虽然不够精确，但仍然有用。

sentences.en: They'll never be able to nail down whether Joe Biden is going to win Georgia or lose it by four or win it by four.
sentences.zh: 它们永远无法确定乔·拜登究竟会以四个百分点赢得佐治亚州，还是以四个百分点输掉该州。

sentences.en: Like, they're just not that good, but they're good enough to flag that something happened in Georgia and that's useful to us.
sentences.zh: 就像是，它们没那么准，但足以提醒我们佐治亚州发生了某些情况，这对我们来说是有用的。

sentences.en: Another possibility is that they're so imprecise that they're no longer useful.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是，它们太不精确了，以至于不再有任何用处。

sentences.en: It's like, all right, we got these polls showing Biden up eight points, but in our political era, the range of possible outcomes in national elections is pretty tight.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，我们看到这些民调显示拜登领先八个百分点，但在我们这个政治时代，全国大选可能出现的结果范围其实很窄。

sentences.en: In my lifetime, the whole range of results goes from, what, Bush plus two in 2004 to Clinton plus eight in 1996.
sentences.zh: 在我有生之年，整个结果范围从2004年布什领先两个百分点，到1996年克林顿领先八个百分点不等。

sentences.en: And so if the amount of error in a poll is basically equal to the range of possible results, they may tell us something, but they're just not that useful.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果民调的误差范围基本等同于可能结果的范围，它们或许能告诉我们一些东西，但确实没那么有用。

sentences.en: In any given election, either side can win and you can't rule out anything and you didn't get that much out of it.
sentences.zh: 在任何一场选举中，任何一方都可能获胜，你无法排除任何可能性，所以你从中得不到太多有价值的信息。

sentences.en: Third possibility is that the polls are so wrong that they're counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 第三种可能性是，民调错得离谱，以至于适得其反。

sentences.en: They're not just useless, but they give an actively misleading picture of the country that we live in.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅毫无用处，反而对我们所处的国家给出了一个极具误导性的图景。

sentences.en: That would be really bad if true.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，那情况就非常糟糕了。

sentences.en: Okay, so now I need to know, where do you fall on this spectrum?
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在我需要知道，你在这个光谱中处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Imprecise, but directionally useful, useless, but we can live with them, really bad and misleading and counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 是不够精确但方向有用，是毫无用处但我们能凑合用，还是非常糟糕、具有误导性且适得其反？

sentences.en: Because it feels like for a lot of people, number three is kind of where we may be living right now.
sentences.zh: 因为对很多人来说，感觉我们现在可能正处于第三种情况。

sentences.en: Where is your head?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: And I think there are definitely elements of the polling error this year and in 2016 that fall into the counterproductive category.
sentences.zh: 我认为今年和2016年的民调误差中，确实存在属于“适得其反”类别的因素。

sentences.en: You know, in Ohio and Iowa, Joe Biden decided to spend, you know, late parts of his campaign, final stop in Cleveland on the day before the election.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在俄亥俄州和艾奥瓦州，乔·拜登决定在竞选后期投入资源，你知道，选举前一天还在克利夫兰做了最后停留。

sentences.en: That's outright counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 那完全是适得其反的。

sentences.en: It's also counterproductive for readers in the electorate.
sentences.zh: 这对选民读者来说也是适得其反的。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: there are cases where political activists make decisions to spend money on long-shot Senate races like South Carolina Senate or the Kansas Senate race or the Alaska Senate race where people just put their energies into the wrong spot.
sentences.zh: 有些情况下，政治活动家决定把钱花在像南卡罗来纳州参议院竞选、堪萨斯州参议院竞选或阿拉斯加州参议院竞选这种胜算渺茫的比赛上，人们只是把精力放错了地方。

sentences.en: There's also a toll on people's trust in institutions.
sentences.zh: 这对人们对机构的信任也有损害。

sentences.en: Polling is an inherently uncertain thing.
sentences.zh: 民调本质上是一件不确定的事情。

sentences.en: And so we do expect, to some extent, that readers appreciate that, you know, polls can be off and it shouldn't undermine the credibility of other things that we have to say or do,
sentences.zh: 所以我们在一定程度上确实希望读者能理解，你知道，民调可能会有偏差，这不应该削弱我们所说或所做的其他事情的可信度，

sentences.en: which could be more based on the firmest facts.
sentences.zh: 那些事情可能更多是基于最确凿的事实。

sentences.en: But I think that it does undermine the credibility of our ability to communicate to readers that we understand the difference between something that we know to be true and something that is a best estimate.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这确实削弱了我们向读者传达我们理解“已知事实”与“最佳估计”之间区别的能力的可信度。

sentences.en: But you didn't answer my question.
sentences.zh: 但你没有回答我的问题。

sentences.en: Where do you fall?
sentences.zh: 你处于什么位置？

sentences.en: I'm really, look, I think that for— I really am torn.
sentences.zh: 我真的，听着，我认为对于——我真的很纠结。

sentences.en: I think the alternatives to public polling are pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 我认为公共民调的替代方案相当糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, we're just stuck to talk to our neighbors and our like-minded friends.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们只能和邻居以及志同道合的朋友交谈。

sentences.en: We wouldn't really have any idea of what's happening in the rest of the country, potentially.
sentences.zh: 我们可能根本不知道全国其他地方正在发生什么。

sentences.en: So that's tough to accept.
sentences.zh: 所以这很难接受。

sentences.en: Let's revisit this after the autopsy.
sentences.zh: 让我们在复盘之后再来讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, if we go through the data and we find that there are things that we can fix,
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果我们仔细检查数据，发现有一些我们可以修正的地方，

sentences.en: then we'll make those changes and evaluate whether we think we're still in the imperfect but useful category.
sentences.zh: 那么我们会做出这些改变，并评估我们是否认为自己仍然处于“不完美但有用”的类别中。

sentences.en: And then we might continue to do some amount of public polling in the future.
sentences.zh: 然后我们可能会在未来继续进行一定程度的公共民调。

sentences.en: But if we conclude that we don't think we can fix these things, then we have a really hard choice, which is whether to abandon the enterprise altogether,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们得出结论，认为无法修正这些问题，那么我们就面临一个非常艰难的选择，那就是是否完全放弃这项事业，

sentences.en: which has some important costs.
sentences.zh: 这会带来一些重要的代价。

sentences.en: Because if you don't have a read on the attitudes of the electorate, you know, I think we're left with alternatives that are not very good.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你无法解读选民的态度，你知道，我认为我们剩下的替代方案并不好。

sentences.en: And I think it does matter to understand where the American people are at.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为了解美国民众的想法确实很重要。

sentences.en: I think it's important the way this democracy works.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对这个民主国家的运作方式很重要。

sentences.en: But if we can't get there, then we can't get there.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们做不到，那就是做不到。

sentences.en: And we would have to reevaluate what we'll do going forward.
sentences.zh: 我们将不得不重新评估未来该怎么做。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, I look forward to hearing what you learn.
sentences.zh: 好吧，内特，我很期待听到你的研究结果。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: I want to spend a few minutes this morning talking about what we saw last week, where we are now, and where our great country will go from here.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我想花几分钟谈谈我们上周所见的情况，我们现在的处境，以及我们伟大的国家未来将走向何方。

sentences.en: In a speech from the Capitol on Monday,
sentences.zh: 周一在国会大厦发表讲话时，

sentences.en: Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell threw his support behind President Trump's refusal to concede the election and declined to recognize President-elect Joe Biden's victory.
sentences.zh: 参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔支持特朗普总统拒绝承认选举结果，并拒绝承认当选总统乔·拜登的胜利。

sentences.en: President Trump is 100% within his rights to look into allegations of irregularities and weigh his legal options.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统完全有权调查违规指控并权衡他的法律选择。

sentences.en: McConnell mocked Democrats for calling on Trump to accept the results of the election.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔嘲讽民主党人呼吁特朗普接受选举结果，

sentences.en: saying that many of them had never recognized Trump's victory four years ago.
sentences.zh: 称他们中的许多人在四年前也从未承认过特朗普的胜利。

sentences.en: That message prompted a scolding from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.
sentences.zh: 这一言论招致了参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默的斥责。

sentences.en: Joe Biden won this election fair and square.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登光明正大地赢得了这次选举。

sentences.en: Republican leaders must unequivocally condemn the president's rhetoric and work to ensure the peaceful transfer of power on January 20th.
sentences.zh: 共和党领导人必须明确谴责总统的言论，并努力确保1月20日权力的和平过渡。

sentences.en: But too many, including the Republican leader, have been silent or sympathetic to the president's fantasies.
sentences.zh: 但太多人，包括共和党领袖，要么保持沉默，要么对总统的幻想表示同情。

sentences.en: And the drugmaker Pfizer announced that an early analysis of large-scale human testing has found that its coronavirus vaccine is more than 90% effective in preventing infection.
sentences.zh: 制药商辉瑞公司宣布，对大规模人体测试的早期分析发现，其新冠疫苗在预防感染方面的有效性超过90%。

sentences.en: A highly promising result that could make it a leading candidate for federal approval.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有希望的结果，可能使其成为联邦批准的主要候选疫苗。

sentences.en: The clinical trial is not complete and the results could change.
sentences.zh: 临床试验尚未完成，结果可能会有变化。

sentences.en: But so far, the company said, no serious safety concerns have been observed.
sentences.zh: 但该公司表示，到目前为止，尚未观察到严重的安全性问题。

sentences.en: Pfizer said that it would ask the FDA for emergency authorization for the vaccine later this month.
sentences.zh: 辉瑞表示，将于本月晚些时候向美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）申请该疫苗的紧急使用授权。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让你的客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会因为喝醉而昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
